title: blower_motor_bench_tests_lot4471_DO_NOT_LOSE.xlsx
body: Bench data, 40 units sampled from blower motor Lot 4471 (Ohio plant, installed across the fleet over the last 18 months). Thermal cutoff trips at 3.6 to 4.1 hours of continuous wave under summer load, versus 11+ hours for Lot 4102 and Lot 4200. Housing temp at trip: 84C. Motor restarts clean after 40 min cooling, then trips again. Conclusion in plain English: 4471 runs hot. It is the lot, not the fleet. If anyone ever proposes pulling all 11,000 tube men over this, show them column D and charge them for the coffee. Units on 4471: 1,850.

title: Fleet Reliability Review, November
meta: Attendees: Gary Baszo, Walt Brzezinski, Dale Withers. Transcribed by MeetingMinder.
body: WALT: Field reports say random units cutting out after long runs. DALE: AutoPlex will notice. Deb notices everything. GARY: It is not random. It is Lot 4471. Eighteen hundred fifty units, installed the last eighteen months, thermal cutoff on the blower. The rest of the fleet could wave through a heat dome. WALT: So a scoped swap. GARY: Scoped swap. Pull 4471, leave the rest standing. A tube man's whole job is getting back up; let us not lay off ten thousand of them for one lot's mistake. ACTION: Gary to file bench data. Status: filed, allegedly.

title: RE: RE: your overflow problem (and my overflow problem)
body: Gary. Like I told Gusty over cards: our industrial helium allocation runs a structural surplus in summer, everyone welds in the fall. The contract has an assignment clause, Section 6, written by my lawyer nephew who owed me a favor. If Grand Inflation ever gets pinched, the allocation assigns to you at 1.4x list. That is not gouging, that is friendship with a service charge. Say hello to the big swan. Marv. P.S. We are gas men, Gary. Nobody understands us, and when we explain ourselves, everyone laughs at the voice.

title: WHERE_THE_OTHER_HELIUM_IS.doc
body: If you are reading this, the allocation got cut and everyone upstairs is breathing into a paper bag, which at least is not a helium waste. Options, in order: 1) Tri-State Welding Gas, Marv Kowalik. Assignable allocation, Section 6, 1.4x list. Summer surplus is structural: welders weld in the fall. One phone call and a signature. 2) Stadium draw is the swing capacity: dark-store rigs cut game-day helium 80 percent and nobody in section 130 can tell. 3) Suspend B2C party kit fills. Children forgive. Liquidated damages do not. 4) There is no option four. The parade flies.

title: Post-mortem: the September squeeze
meta: Attendees: Gary Baszo, Gusty Womplerton Jr. Handwritten, digitized 2026.
body: GUSTY JR: We nearly missed Frostbite Falls over a helium invoice. GARY: We fly on contracts, not on hope. Get a second source with an assignment clause, keep it warm with a Christmas card every year. GUSTY JR: Who? GARY: Marv at Tri-State. He owes your father from cards and he over-ordered for fall welding season like he does every year. Helium is the one supplier relationship where, if it goes bad, everyone's voice gets funny in the meeting about it.

title: who actually signs at AutoPlex (save this, Dale)
body: Dale. The org chart says VP Marketing owns our contract. The org chart is a bedtime story. Deb Kowalski, fleet procurement, has final signature on every dollar that touches the dealerships. I know because in 2019 the VP approved the inflatable gorilla program and Deb un-approved it in one email with no adjectives. Send your uptime reports to Deb. Copy the VP if it makes him feel aerodynamic. And never promise Deb a date you got from hope instead of the ERP; that woman can smell an uninflated number through a phone line.

title: parade_wind_rules_plain_english.txt
body: Section 11.3 of the Harvest Parade agreement, translated from lawyer: sustained 23 mph or gusts 34 mph is the line. At the line, a joint go/no-go call at 06:00 parade morning, us and parade ops together, names attached, in writing. Below the line you can still fly a modified launch: fewer balloons, low-altitude rig, more handlers per line. The balloons do not read the contract. The wind does not read the forecast. The 06:00 call is where humans earn their salary. I have flown 39 parades and scrubbed 2, and the scrubs are the ones I sleep well about.

title: Pre-parade wind briefing with Harvest Parade Partners
meta: Attendees: Gary Baszo, Colleen Marsh (Harvest Parade Partners). Transcribed by MeetingMinder.
body: COLLEEN: How do you want to run the morning call if Thursday is marginal? GARY: You bring the forecast, I bring the riggers' hands. Colleen decides with data and she decides early; do not bring her vibes at 06:00, bring her numbers at 05:45. COLLEEN: And if it is inside the envelope but trending wrong? GARY: Then we fly nine balloons low instead of sixteen balloons proud. A parade with fewer balloons is still a parade. A balloon in a power line is a career.

title: RE: the expedite button in AirWare
body: Walt. The consultants added an expedite_cert button to AirWare because their spec said configurable workflow. I want it on the record: the 14-day safety certification is not a workflow, it is the reason no child has ever been hurt by our products. The button skips QA. We do not press it. We staple the reason to the wall: seam failures show up on day 9 to day 12 of soak testing. A cert you expedite is a recall you scheduled. If demand screams, we add shifts, we add Fiesta, we ship honest dates. We do not press the button. Not for a pop star. Not for anybody.

title: rigger_bench_status_MY_LAST_UPDATE.txt
body: Level IV Master Riggers as of my retirement: me (out Friday), Yolanda Cruz, Pete Duffy. Sam Okafor is 5 months from Level IV and better on knots than I was at his age; his altitude math still needs a second pair of eyes. Certification takes 18 months because the big balloons take 18 months to show you their moods. Two riggers minimum per giant balloon on parade day, per Section 7.2. After Friday the bench is three deep counting Sam's paperwork. Plan launches accordingly and do not let anyone with a clipboard say a drone can hold a line. A drone cannot feel a gust coming through its boots.

title: colossal_swan_field_notes.doc
body: Colossal Swan XL, field notes. Ninety percent of deflation complaints are the valve cap seated a quarter-turn shy: tell the customer to listen for the second click. The neck seam is rated to 40 percent over spec; the wing seams are not, so bulk-order customers stacking them in trucks in July heat will generate tickets, and the tickets will say defective, and the swan will be innocent. The swan is usually innocent. Check the valve first, apologize second, refund third.

title: Frostbite Falls: cold-rated only, I mean it
body: Team. Frostbite Falls is in January. Standard vinyl goes brittle at those temps and a brittle balloon does not deflate, it abdicates. Cold-rated skins only, valve grease rated to minus 30, and brief the handlers that helium contracts in the cold: the balloon that looked underfilled in the hangar is correct on the street. Every January somebody tops one off indoors and then acts surprised outside. The gas laws are not company policy, but they outrank it.

title: Gary Baszo exit interview (part 1 of 1, he said one was plenty)
meta: Attendees: Gary Baszo, HR. Transcribed by MeetingMinder.
body: HR: Forty-three years. What do you want the next generation to know? GARY: Check the valve first. Get the helium in writing. The org chart is not the decision chart; the graph I gave you is. The 14 days are the product. And when the wind is marginal, the brief can be perfect but a person signs the launch. HR: Any regrets? GARY: I let go of a swan in 1987 and I still look for it on clear days. HR: Anything else? GARY: Tell them the graph knows what I know. It does not know what I would do. That part they have to earn.

title: what the graph is (and is not)
body: Gale. They finished digitizing me. The graph has every relationship I could remember, and this archive has every file, message, and meeting behind it. Between them, whoever asks a real question gets a real answer, which is more than you could reliably get from me before coffee. Two warnings. One: knowing is not deciding; do not let anyone hide a decision inside a lookup. Two: the archive contains my jokes. I have reviewed them. They hold air. Gary.

title: #helium
body: safety refresher, summer edition: helium is lighter than air, lighter than deadlines, lighter than your excuses. it is the only inventory that files its own shrinkage report by leaving. seal the manifolds, log the draw, and stop doing the voice at the fill station, Kevin, the meeting was about you.

title: Line 2 capacity, if it ever goes crazy
meta: Attendees: Gary Baszo, Walt Brzezinski. Transcribed by MeetingMinder.
body: WALT: Corporate wants a surge plan on file before you leave. GARY: Line 2 does 1,200 swans a week on two shifts, 4,100 on three before people and welders get sloppy. Past that you call Fiesta, audit is current, five-day ramp. You do not touch the cert. You publish the honest date, and the honest date is the one the ERP gives you, not the one marketing dreams. WALT: And if demand goes to forty times? GARY: Then it is a good week to make joy that holds air, and a bad week to make promises that do not.
